text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.
BARLEY SALES - Cyprus bought 25,000 tonnes of feed barley from Crissel Greece at $136.49 per tonne, C and F, Cyprus's grain commission said, for December or January shipment.

WHEAT BRAN SALE - South Korea's Korea Feed Association bought 22,000 tonnes of wheat bran pellets for arrival on December 20, traders said. Traders said South Korean Trading house LG International Corp sold 10,000 tonnes at $130.50 per tonne sourced from Sri Lanka, and Daehan Flour Mills Co Ltd sold the remaining 12,000 at $124.70 sourced from Indonesia.

WHEAT TENDERS - Two Philippine flour mills rejected bids for 35,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat because prices were high, traders said. The mills sought 25,000 tonnes of dark northern spring wheat and 10,000 tonnes of western white wheat for December-January shipment.

- Turkey will invite bids December 10 to import 200,000 tonnes of red and white milling wheat on a three-year credit basis, a grain official said. He said the imports would be from either the United States, Australia, Argentina or any European Union member country.

WHEAT TENDERS - Tunisia launched a tender on Tuesday for 100,000 tonnes of optional-origin soft wheat to be shipped in January and February, European grain traders said. The tender will be awarded on December 5, they said.

- Taiwan Flour Mills Association will tender Wednesday for 72,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat for last-half December shipment, traders said. Shipment would be from the Pacific Northwest. The tender is on behalf of the Taiwan wheat companies including President Enterprise, Tai Yu Products, Chia Hsin, Formosa Oilseed and Lien Hwa Industry.
SOYBEAN TENDER - South Korea is to tender for 55,000 tonnes of No.1 optional-origin soybeans late Wednesday for December-January shipment.
LENTIL TENDER - Syria offered 9,500 tonnes of lentils for export. December 16 was set as final date for bids and results would be announced on December 17.
MARKET TALK - The European Union cut distant import duties on durum wheat from 7.65 Ecus per tonne to 1.07 Ecus per tonne effective December 4, the European Commission said on Tuesday.

MARKET TALK - Iraq has unfrozen $70 million worth of funds in a deal arranged by an Austrian firm in exchange for substantial commodities purchases, Jordanian traders said Tuesday. The deal includes supplying Iraq with 160,000-180,000 tonnes of U.K. and Argentine wheat, about 75,000 tonnes of Brazilian sugar and 33,000 tonnes of Vietnamese rice. Shipments are for November, December and January.

MARKET TALK - USDA said Tuesday it made vegetable oils and frozen or chilled meats available for sale to Estonia under the short-term GSM-102 export credit guarantee program. USDA said total credits for Estonia remained $6 million. Eligible vegetable oils were soybean, sunflower, cottonseed, corn and peanut oils. Eligible frozen or chilled meats were beef, poultry, pork, sheep and offals.
